a daily basis as indicated by D1 in the title block.
This procedure documents is the 1st. level of maintenance performed on this type 
of transformer.

items: A work permit must be issued.

Maintenance Record Data Sheet or mark on a 
 copy of this document is required.

Read and record the valves of the oil on the oil level
 gauges of the transformer and tap-changer and check that the oil levels
 are. Correct for the atmospheric temp.

Read and record oil temperatures and check that the
 maximum temperature is acceptable by comparing it with past entries in the
 inspection log.

Read and record load (MW and MVAR) from control room input
 voltage and output voltage check that load and voltage must be kept with
 in the specified limits, which are in the instruction manual. Oil
 temperature can be record from the thermo signal and be sure that the
 temperature on the thermo-signal Is less than 65c (65 o C alarm
 signal 75c trip).

Check the porcelain for cracking and other damage check
 that there is no leakage of oil.

Check that there is no over heating of the terminals for
 heat discoloration using binoculars.

Visually check the pressure of oil on the pressure gauges
 for 500 & 220& 132 kV for bushings and compare it the chart of
 pressure and temperature according to fig.1.

Check for leakage from the transformer tank radiators,
 valves, pipes, gauges, gasket joints welds.

The silica-gel Absorbent inside the breather bottle is
 normally magenta blue, but rarus:
 - Audible Noises
 - Loose by parts
 - Cooling equipment.

Check that the brake of the wheels of the transformer on
 the railway is fixed.

text:
Introduction
This procedure details the equipment Inspection steps I1, which are performed on 
a daily basis as indicated by D1 in the title block.
This procedure documents is the 1st. level of maintenance performed on this type 
of transformer.
Safety
Precautions
A work permit must be issued.
Tools
and Equipment
Maintenance Record Data Sheet or mark on a 
 copy of this document is required.
Work to be carried out
Oil Level
Read and record the valves of the oil on the oil level
 gauges of the transformer and tap-changer and check that the oil levels
 are. Correct for the atmospheric temp.
Transformer
 Temperatures, Load And Voltages
Read and record oil temperatures and check that the
 maximum temperature is acceptable by comparing it with past entries in the
 inspection log.
Read and record load (MW and MVAR) from control room input
 voltage and output voltage check that load and voltage must be kept with
 in the specified limits, which are in the instruction manual. Oil
 temperature can be record from the thermo signal and be sure that the
 temperature on the thermo-signal Is less than 65c (65 o C alarm
 signal 75c trip).
Bushings
Check the porcelain for cracking and other damage check
 that there is no leakage of oil.
Check that there is no over heating of the terminals for
 heat discoloration using binoculars.
Visually check the pressure of oil on the pressure gauges
 for 500 & 220& 132 kV for bushings and compare it the chart of
 pressure and temperature according to fig.1.
Oil Leakage
Check for leakage from the transformer tank radiators,
 valves, pipes, gauges, gasket joints welds.
Dehydrating Breather
The silica-gel Absorbent inside the breather bottle is
 normally magenta blue, but rarus:
 - Audible Noises
 - Loose by parts
 - Cooling equipment.
Check that the brake of the wheels of the transformer on
 the railway is fixed.
